answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. Votes count only from deposits that have aged through a challenge period; if an identity is caught endorsing fabricated work, its stake is forfeited. Splitting one deposit across a hundred Sybils does not create more voting weight, while acquiring many independent deposits ties up real capital and risks loss. The orchard can label a kernel task “comet,” but those names cannot substitute for collateral.
